author: ogalush
body:
## 目的 パフォーマンス改善 （暫定） ## 概要 接続数 100名+でトップページの閲覧がしづらい（場合によっては見えない）という問題が発生しています。 実装を確認したところ トップページ閲覧時に `initdb()` で `CREATE TABLE IF EXISTS` などを実施しているように見えています。 https://github.com/kita-develop/discover-stocks/blob/main/app.py#L7 ↓ https://github.com/kita-develop/discover-stocks/blob/main/utils/db.py#L10-L53 このため、トップページ閲覧時にトランザクションを取得して遅くなっているかも？ という仮定の基、トランザクションを軽くしたいと思います。 ### トランザクション管理の変更 [SQLite のパフォーマンスに関するベスト プラクティス ](https://developer.android.com/topic/performance/sqlite-performance-best-practices?hl=ja) を見て、 * write-ahead log 書き込みを有効化 * 同期モードを緩和する の対策が手っ取り早く出来そうに見えるので実装します。 意味合いとしては |Key|Value|Note| |---|---|---| |journal_mode| `DELETE -> WAL` |DELETE: トランザクション終了時にロールバックジャーナルを削除する設定
↓
WAL: ログ先行書き込み（WAL）ということで追記型へ変更
ということでファイルの削除によるファイルロックを減らす。
Ref: https://sqlite.org/pragma.html#pragma_journal_mode| |synchronous| `FULL -> NORMAL`|FULL: commitタイミングで `fsync` 完了まで待つ。
↓
NORMAL: 重要なタイミングで同期するものの、 FULLモードよりは頻度は少なくなる。
（＝レスポンス高速化）
かつ、 `WAL mode is safe from corruption with synchronous=NORMAL,... ` ということなので破損からも保護されるとのこと。

ということなので、クラッシュ時の安全性は若干下がるものの、クラッシュ頻度もそうなさそうなのでパフォーマンスへ若干寄せるイメージです。
Ref: https://sqlite.org/pragma.html#pragma_synchronous| ### データベース管理メニューへの追加 上述のWAL モードにするとログ書き込み用に `surbey.db{,-shm,-wal}` の3ファイルが出来るため、 チェックポイント(postgresとかだとvacuumdb相当？)できる様に `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(FULL)` するページを増やしました。 ## 効果 パフォーマンスコマンドの `wrk` で、ローカルで試せる程度 (127接続, 127スレッド, 60秒)で試したところ 以下の様に心持ち早くなったかなくらいの感じです。 Requests/sec: +9.3% ``` % echo '4382.06 / 4008.54 * 100' | bc -l 109.31810584402301087100 ``` ローカルで試した程度の差分なので、 リリースした際に効果がどの程度出るかは試してみないとなぁという印象です。 （誤差程度の効果だったらスイマセンmm） 変更前 ``` % wrk -t127 -c127 -d60s 'http://127.0.0.1:8501/?page=top&date=20250323' Running 1m test @ http://127.0.0.1:8501/?page=top&date=20250323 127 threads and 127 connections Thread Stats Avg Stdev Max +/- Stdev Latency 31.42ms 4.45ms 86.44ms 96.19% Req/Sec 31.76 5.29 80.00 69.13% 240935 requests in 1.00m, 510.79MB read Socket errors: connect 1, read 0, write 0, timeout 0 Requests/sec: 4008.54 Transfer/sec: 8.50MB ``` → `Requests/sec: 4008.54` 変更後 ``` % wrk -t127 -c127 -d60s 'http://127.0.0.1:8501/?page=top&date=20250323' Running 1m test @ http://127.0.0.1:8501/?page=top&date=20250323 127 threads and 127 connections Thread Stats Avg Stdev Max +/- Stdev Latency 28.73ms 2.58ms 61.12ms 96.84% Req/Sec 34.76 5.23 181.00 44.77% 263380 requests in 1.00m, 558.37MB read Socket errors: connect 1, read 0, write 0, timeout 0 Requests/sec: 4382.06 Transfer/sec: 9.29MB ``` → `Requests/sec: 4382.06` ## スクリーンショット ### WAL変更 → `survey.db` から3ファイルへ増えたのでモード変更を確認済 ``` % ls -al survey.db* -rw-r--r-- 1 ogalush staff 606208 3 23 05:04 survey.db -rw-r--r-- 1 ogalush staff 32768 3 23 05:06 survey.db-shm -rw-r--r-- 1 ogalush staff 0 3 23 05:04 survey.db-wal ``` ### データベース整理画面 → データベース管理画面に「データベース整理」ボタンをつけました。 ## その他 ChatGPTで調べた感じだと、Streamlit自体が1プロセス1スレッドのフレームワークという風に回答があったので、 おそらくパフォーマンス改善の根本対応は ``` As Is ・StreamLitとDB (Sqlite)が同じインスタンスに乗っている状態 ↓ To Be ・StreamLit * 複数インスタンス + DBをSQLite → MySQLへ換装（複数インスタンスで共有できる様に） ・もしくは、マルチスレッド対応フレームワークへの変更（パッと思い浮かばずですが） ``` という感じで、横方向へスケールアウトする構成変更がいるのかなぁ、、という理解をしています。 ただ、そこまでやろうとすると既存からの改修量も多く、趣味というよりも案件対応になってくるのかなととも思ったので、 今できる範囲でということでPRしました。

author: wschurman
body:
# Why

This is part 3 of #201. This PR adds support for composite field loading.

Closes #201.

# How

1. Add a new composite field and composite field value holder. (holder concept introduced in parent PR)
2. Add new loader methods.
3. Fix the knex database adapter since loading via `ANY` is not possible for composite columns.

# Knex change

This turned out to be a change needed at the 11th hour after much testing, and is somewhat a pain. Previous comments on architecture noted:
> WHERE IN makes a mess of the query stats table (for each cardinality of arrays there's a separate entry). We use WHERE = ANY so that the query shape is the same whether there are 2, 3, or 100 values to match.

Unfortunately, postgres doesn't support `ANY` on these tuple like types (composite) without explicit type casting. The precise error thrown is `input of anonymous composite types is not implemented`.

I looked into using a `unnest` trick as described https://blog.jakubholy.net/2023/pg-select-where-match-on-list-of-tuples/ but it also got very messy.

So I ended up just using `WHERE IN` for the composite loads since it's the simplest.

# Test Plan

Add a lot of new tests.

author: anuskuss
body:
I want to turn `SERVFAIL`s into `NXDOMAIN` so my client cache the response (you're not supposed to cache `SERVFAIL`s at all or for [no longer than 5 minutes](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2308#section-7.1)).

The easiest way to achive that (besides #443) would be to just `fail-back` to a `static-responder` with `rcode=3` and `ns=[". 3600 IN SOA . . 0 3600 3600 3600 3600"]`. But I don't want to keep using the `static-responder` and 1 second is too long for switching back, so this change allows you to use it for 0 seconds (i.e. only switch to the `static-resonder` once).

author: blishko
body:
Edge inlining refers to a transformation where we detect if an edge has at most one feasible predecessor.
If there is no feasible predecessor, the edge can be safely removed from the graph, without affecting reachability.
If there is a single feasible predecessor, the edge can be merged with the predecessor. We can remove the original edge but must keep the predecessor, because there might be other outgoing edges from the original edge's source.
We also do not want to inline if the predecessor is a loop. That would basically meant peeling off one iteration from the loop, and that could continue for a long time.

By feasibility we mean that the conjunction of the labels of the edge and its predecessor (after appropriate variable renaming) is satisfiable.
However, we do not check satisfiability by querying an SMT solver, instead we use light-weight check where we collect constant values of the common state variables and see if they contradict each other or not.

body:
### Description
Changed a lot here, in this branch nodes don't use templates and use visits for type handling instead. Changed nodes so they have strings for inputs/outputs and make lookups in a map instead for their tensors. The model sorts the nodes topologically to execute the infer in order. It sorts the nodes into layers/levels so that each node in each layer/level can be executed in parallel in the future. Also made tests for the parser and model using a very simple model. 

Many nodes are already implemented here but many new ones need to be added! Also some interface methods might be useful for the model class to make inputting data easier.

### Issue
Closes #55

author: kenny516
body:
This pull request introduces several significant changes to the `EvaluationCrm` project, including the addition of new controllers, entity models, and updates to the database context and project file. The most important changes are outlined below:

### Controllers

* Added a new `RoleController` to manage roles within the application. This controller includes a dependency injection for `RoleService` and an `Index` action to list all roles.

### Entity Models

* Added multiple new entity models to represent various aspects of the CRM system, including `ContractSetting`, `Customer`, `CustomerLoginInfo`, `EmailTemplate`, `Employee`, `File`, `GoogleDriveFile`, `LeadAction`, `LeadSetting`, `OauthUser`, `Role`, `TicketSetting`, `TriggerContract`, `TriggerLead`, `TriggerTicket`, and `User`. Each model includes properties and relationships relevant to the CRM system. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f14649827b5f7ada32d53d3e1b4a625b93bfa9182e7c4544dee8e50260219327R1-R53) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8855d42e1a6dd33539df88edab1e833ba3b8c01a0580430a8b3831e8e4284402R1-R49) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-213d8881a3b531dffd9c58683a5a564fff157c98602ab5b7ef38296734617b8cR1-R25) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-f8483b1cbba16ed34c883938b09448a3bdbc22c0c91a658dcbc49281c0237995R1-R49) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-15040c5f52cc96a44a5f21a546b55f409bfa77ffb3fd61459ada1201c3280cb5R1-R21) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-0a995de7e0bed3d0bc4952508c9b7e0c8140f5488da5c1c58883ee8fa296d780R1-R23) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-75de51f9bfe82ed06cb2b757da0c40d669560c303a33855cd4730703e7632950R1-R21) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-c0a9be4d23036ef0308df55a8e661b2f8eaf3961425e3978c0286d4e87f7636fR1-R17) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-2ccbc30b7a00c27e92dc945cd15b48a840819fcbbebeb66aafcfab02e71a45abR1-R41) [[10]](diffhunk://#diff-6e07f5deb9dcc8b777e133e3e8fff99211690f889ca23d0da82caa9c91926dd5R1-R29) [[11]](diffhunk://#diff-605b130dc7be6c41fc0852826bf143559bdaf7ccebca6b82c28aac28dfabb9f6R1-R15) [[12]](diffhunk://#diff-67f2ee2b7104e64e5e690e9fe522cbefedc14f85e7ecffc674bfa41d89887c5cR1-R41) [[13]](diffhunk://#diff-58e4e7073c2f3abbca8f3cddc1fa2a93540ce73ace7a00e4e87136b6d62a0e7dR1-R43) [[14]](diffhunk://#diff-7ddbad9ef1124bae83ba742220a4b41c0056e6d394d9190f47e884eff890d44cR1-R43) [[15]](diffhunk://#diff-554409a77f4856690ddd1974eb680fcc5331d777063573da4aac1784e639838cR1-R31) [[16]](diffhunk://#diff-413e87ccb82b8c4ca51527fcb660440a3e6aaa2258a70ae22ae7f4fdfd859976R1-R53)

### Database Context

* Updated the `ApplicationDbContext` to include a `DbSet<Role>` for managing roles in the database. This change supports the new role management functionality.

### Project File

* Updated the `EvaluationCrm.csproj` file to include new package references for `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore`, `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Tools`, and `Pomelo.EntityFrameworkCore.MySql`. These packages are necessary for Entity Framework Core and MySQL support.

These changes collectively enhance the functionality and structure of the `EvaluationCrm` project, enabling better role management and expanding the entity models to support various CRM features.

body: ### Summary This PR implements live electric field readouts at the cursor position within the canvas, enhancing the user’s ability to analyze dynamic field behavior precisely and intuitively. Closes #64 --- ### ✅ Features Implemented - **Live electric field vector display** (`Ex`, `Ey`) in the bottom-right corner of the canvas. - Field values update in real-time as the user moves the mouse across the canvas. - Scaled values are shown in **kN/C** for readability. - Inverted Y-component (`Ey`) to match the visual direction of field vectors. - Minimal performance overhead using direct DOM interaction and reactive updates. --- ### 🧩 Technical Details - Added a new utility: `getNetElectricFieldAtPoint` in `mathUtils.ts` to aggregate total field from all charges. - Registered a `mousemove` listener in `PixiCanvas.vue` to capture cursor position and compute field values. - Rendered a visually unobtrusive `.field-readout` overlay in the UI corner. - Applied value scaling (`/ 1e3`) to convert from raw N/C to **kN/C**. --- ### 📸 Screenshots ### 🧪 Tested On - Chrome, Firefox, Safari (desktop) - Varying charge magnitudes and positions - Edge cases like overlapping or near-zero field zones --- ### 📝 Notes - Currently implemented for **electric mode** only. - Magnetic field/vector readouts could follow a similar pattern in a future enhancement.

body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive role and permission management system, including new controllers, middleware, models, and database migrations. The changes are designed to enhance the application's ability to manage user roles and permissions effectively.

### Controllers:
* Added `PermissionController` to manage permissions, including methods for listing, creating, updating, and deleting permissions.
* Added `RoleController` to manage roles, including methods for listing, creating, updating, and deleting roles.

### Middleware:
* Introduced `CheckPermission` middleware to handle permission checks for incoming requests.
* Introduced `CheckRole` middleware to handle role checks for incoming requests.

### Models:
* Created `Permission` model with relationships to `User` and `Role` models.
* Created `Role` model with methods to manage permissions and relationships to `User` and `Permission` models.
* Updated `User` model to include methods for role management.

### Database Migrations:
* Added migrations for creating `roles`, `permissions`, `user_role`, and `role_permission` tables. author: kjkent
body:
From https://github.com/ventoy/Ventoy/issues/3174#issue-2940384521:

> - Having nested if statements in wait_and_create_part() corrupts the intended logic. If the first condition (for $vPART1) passes but the second (for $vPART2) fails, the else doesn't trigger, leading to missed waits, and then a missed sanity check at the end that allows execution to continue
> - Using ls | grep -q '^b' to check for block devices (again in wait_and_create_part()) is fragile: it's not uncommon for ls to be aliased or options set that may prevent 'b' from reliably being the first letter of the output for a valid block device. Also, the partitions are being checked for presence, then immediately checked again, and if they don't enumerate the second time then mknod is being called which could cause further device re-enumeration
> - The quick succession of having the partitions be altered and checked, sequentially and inconsistently due to the first point, is causing a race condition that allows execution to continue when it shouldn't.
> 
> I edited the code to use partprobe (provided by parted, which the project already depends on) to inform the kernel of any device changes, slowed the loop down and removed the mknod code, and it worked great afterwards.
>
> Interestingly, as happened in my case, if the device already had a exfat partition 1, from an old ventoy installation or prior use, that old fs signature can persist through the formatting process leading to weird effect. I was experiencing https://github.com/ventoy/Ventoy/issues/1133, on GPT and MBR, but after changing this logic, Windows 11 installation now works fine.

In the end I elected to not remove the `mknod` code as I figured that there may be a legitimate case where it's needed. However, in this PR I edit it to only be called if the partition fs nodes are not found after repeated kernel refreshing, and, after it runs, the device partitions are re-checked before continuing. If this succeeds then the process continues to `mkexfatfs`, and, if not, the user is advised to try re-inserting the USB or retrying with other ports/hardware.

I hope this PR is okay? It's my first to the project and I hope it's helpful in some way.

Closes #3174 and #3256

body: Checklist * [x] Used a [personal fork of the feedstock to propose changes](https://conda-forge.org/docs/maintainer/updating_pkgs.html#forking-and-pull-requests) * [x] Bumped the build number (if the version is unchanged) * [ ] Reset the build number to `0` (if the version changed) * [x] [Re-rendered]( https://conda-forge.org/docs/maintainer/updating_pkgs.html#rerendering-feedstocks ) with the latest `conda-smithy` (Use the phrase @conda-forge-admin, please rerender in a comment in this PR for automated rerendering) * [x] Ensured the license file is being packaged. Currently the cuda and pytorch pins allow cuda versions to based on what's default. E.g. when building version: ``` linux_64_c_compiler_version13cuda_compilercuda-nvcccuda_compiler_version12.6cxx_compiler_version13python3.10.____cpython ``` it ends up with deps like: ``` cuda-cudart: 12.8.90-h5888daf_1 conda-forge cuda-cudart-dev: 12.8.90-h5888daf_1 conda-forge pytorch: 2.6.0-cuda126_mkl_py310_hb403307_302 conda-forge ``` which makes it incompatible with the very cuda 12.6 it's supposed to be using in this build, e.g. ``` $ conda create -n pt2.6-sparse-mismatch conda-forge::python=3.10 conda-forge::cuda-runtime=12.6 conda-forge::pytorch=2.6.0=cuda* conda-forge::pytorch_sparse --dry-run ... ├─ pytorch_sparse 0.6.18 would require │ └─ cuda-cudart >=12.8.57,<13.0a0 , which conflicts with any installable versions previously reported; ``` The deps should be (and is after this patch when testing locally): ``` cuda-cudart: 12.6.77-h5888daf_0 conda-forge cuda-cudart-dev: 12.6.77-h5888daf_0 conda-forge pytorch: 2.6.0-cuda126_mkl_py310_hb403307_302 conda-forge ```

This PR migrates core ramping logic from frontend to backend (signer-service), implementing:
- State machine architecture for ramp flows
- PostgreSQL persistence layer
- Resilient transaction processing
- Phase-based execution handlers

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Frontend -->|API Calls| Backend
    Backend --> PhaseHandler
    PhaseHandler --> Database[(PostgreSQL)]
    PhaseHandler --> SquidRouter
    PhaseHandler --> PolkadotService
    PhaseHandler --> RecoveryWorker
    PhaseHandler -->|Events| Frontend
```

## Key Changes

### Backend Implementation
1. **Phase Handlers System**
   - `signer-service/src/api/services/phases/*`

author: alvaroseparovich
body:
# Optimize CI: Add Playwright Browser Caching

## Overview
This PR adds caching for Playwright browsers and dependencies to significantly improve CI workflow performance. By implementing caching, we can save several minutes on each workflow run.

## Changes Made
- Added browser and dependency caching using GitHub Actions cache for both deployment and PR validation workflows
- Added conditional installation step that only runs when cache is not available
- Maintained the same functionality while improving performance

## Benefits
- Reduces CI execution time by avoiding redundant browser installations
- Improves developer experience with faster PR validations
- Reduces GitHub Actions usage minutes and resource consumption
- Maintains the same test reliability and coverage

## Before/After
Before: Every workflow run would download and install all Playwright browsers and dependencies (~150-300MB)
After: Browsers are cached between runs, only downloaded on cache misses or when dependencies change

## Testing Done
The changes have been tested by ensuring the cache key is properly set to invalidate when dependencies change via the package-lock.json file.

## Notes
Cache storage uses GitHub's cache feature which has a 7-day expiration by default, which is sufficient for our active development cycle.

author: jdpurcell
body:
I noticed this duplicated bit of logic inside the range decoder. Turns out, there's a helper function called `Normalize2` that does the exact same thing and was never even called. This quirk came all the way from the original LZMA C# SDK it seems. I can see why, as with .NET Framework 4.8, attempting to use the helper function results in performance degradation, so someone manually inlined it. But that's not even necessary, as `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]` can be used to achieve the same performance.

But the more interesting part, hence this PR, is that newer JITs (tested with .NET 8.0) don't like the manually inlined version of the code as much; when calling `Normalize2` instead, it seems to get inlined either way (even without the attribute that we put as a hint for .NET 4.8), and the performance is better.

Core i7-6700k (3.2% reduction):

| Method | Mean    | Error    | StdDev   |
|------- |--------:|---------:|---------:|
| Before  | 1.128 s | 0.0018 s | 0.0015 s |
| After  | 1.092 s | 0.0011 s | 0.0009 s |

Apple M3 (11.6% reduction):
| Method | Mean     | Error    | StdDev   |
|------- |---------:|---------:|---------:|
| Before  | 888.9 ms | 16.78 ms | 14.01 ms |
| After  | 785.8 ms |  1.98 ms |  1.85 ms |

That's reduction in overall time to extract the whole archive. Tested with a smaller archive in BenchmarkDotNet and I was honestly in disbelief at first on the M3, but it's real. I also manually benchmarked using the same setup/archive as my first PR, it was a 412MB Qt 7z taking 26+ seconds, and it indeed shaved an entire 3 seconds off the extraction time.

author: neoneko87
body:
This PR introduces a comprehensive modularization of CSS and JavaScript files for the PixTrail web application. Instead of monolithic files (style.css with over 600 lines and main.js with over 1700 lines), functionality is now divided into logical, smaller modules that each fulfill a specific task.

These changes significantly improve maintainability, readability and extensibility of the code without affecting existing functionality.

## Changes

### CSS Modularization

- [x] The CSS has been reorganized following the module pattern:

1. **Base**
   - `variables.css`: Global CSS variables for consistent theming
   - `reset.css`: Basic reset styles for consistent rendering
   - `typography.css`: Text styling and formatting

2. **Layouts**
   - `container.css`: Main container layouts
   - `grid.css`: Grid and flexbox utilities

3. **Modules**
   - Component-specific styles in separate files (header, footer, buttons, forms etc.)
   - Each module focuses on a single UI component
   - Improved naming conventions for better readability

4. **Main CSS**
   - `main.css`: Imports all CSS modules

### JavaScript Modularization

- [x] JavaScript code has been reorganized into a modular, object-oriented structure:

1. **Utils**
   - `domHelpers.js`: DOM manipulation utilities
   - `fileUtils.js`: File handling utilities
   - `gpsUtils.js`: GPS data processing utilities
   - `uiUtils.js`: UI-related utility functions

2. **API**
   - `apiClient.js`: API communication layer

3. **Modules**
   - `dragAndDrop.js`: Drag and drop functionality
   - `exifReader.js`: EXIF metadata extraction
   - `fileUpload.js`: File upload handling
   - `mapVisualization.js`: Map rendering and manipulation
   - `heatmap.js`: Heatmap visualization
   - `clustering.js`: Marker clustering functionality
   - `statistics.js`: Statistics calculation and display
   - `charts.js`: Chart creation and management

4. **Main JS**
   - `main.js`: Entry point that initializes and coordinates all modules

### HTML Updates

- [x] Updated the HTML template to reference the new main CSS and JavaScript files
- [x] Added type="module" to script tag to support ES modules

## Benefits

1. **Improved Maintainability**: Each file has a single responsibility, making it easier to update or fix specific parts without affecting others.

2. **Better Organization**: Files are grouped by functionality, making it easier to find relevant code.

3. **Reduced Code Duplication**: Shared utilities and functions are defined once and reused across components.

4. **Easier Collaboration**: Team members can work on different modules simultaneously with fewer merge conflicts.

5. **Enhanced Extensibility**: New features can be added as new modules without modifying existing code.

## Testing

- [x] All functionality has been manually tested and works as expected
- [x] No changes to the backend were required
- [x] The application maintains backward compatibility with existing data
